rootQAAttribution.reports: Storage/task RPC live, worker offline and disabled controls; original listener PID 91027 on 127.0.0.1:3080; synthetic task cancellation-requested at version 2/epoch 1 with no worker/result.

findings.origin: Proposed lifecycle invalidates setup; retained Panel/setup-card branch makes the new offline read unreachable.
findings.title: Rendered Panel hides readonly worker status during global offline or initially unconfirmed connection
sourceDerivation: apply disconnects setup, worker and task models on loss or missing established generation.
Setup phase becomes offline; Panel returns only setupCard before workerCard can render.
The retained setup-card refresh is disabled in offline phase.
The new enabled worker-status refresh therefore exists only behind an unreachable worker-card branch in this state.
Normal established-generation setup recovery is source supported; this finding concerns rendered offline recovery and truthful unknown initial state.
findings.requiredDisposition: A separately frozen amendment must expose a genuine readonly status/recovery surface in the actual offline/unconfirmed Panel branches, retain disabled decisions, and distinguish absent/unconfirmed state from observed disconnection. It must not fabricate a generation, start a second connection loop, or turn successful RPC into authority.
functionalObligations: Exercise the actual rendered Panel on initial undefined state, observed loss with ordinary RPC live, and whole-store absence.
Show the readonly action is reachable and uses only the original cached-status/setup read.
Show all decisions remain unavailable until genuine complete observables and fresh host reads justify them.

findings.origin: Retained byte-identical a58 worker model; no new worker-model mutation literal.
findings.title: Disconnect can discard uncertainty for a mutation that could already have been submitted
sourceDerivation: run captures a read revision and epoch before an explicitly invoked mutation can call original RPC.
Disconnect increments epoch and invalidation increments revision, aborting the local controller.
The mutation catch records uncertainty only if its read still equals current revision.
The old mutation response/rejection after disconnect cannot set the uncertain marker; invalidation clears previews/grant while retaining worker and execution fields.
Readonly task/status recovery can make retained ready-worker state fresh without establishing the first execution outcome.
Execute controls and model execute check ready worker, absent execution and workerExecute uncertainty; they do not require a fresh grant flag or mandatory Query first.

A later explicit execute request can therefore be offered after the lost response. No automatic retry is introduced. The authoritative backend may reject a duplicate; that does not prove the UI no-repeat-until-established contract.
limits: Pure ordinary client control/RPC-response analysis; no receipt/envelope/security internals were executed or altered.
Local AbortSignal is not evidence of original host noncommit.
The attributed cancelled task with no worker/result does not instantiate this source sequence.
Related later NI3 execution/reconciliation capsules are distinct, unchanged and not imported by this narrow a58 delta.
findings.requiredDisposition: Retain exact actually submitted pending/uncertain operation identity across reset and stale responses; require original readonly/factual reconciliation before re-enabling that mutation. No status refresh may clear uncertainty, infer rollback, or trigger retry/grant/dispatch. Any forward-port requires separately pinned original before bytes and affected independent review.
functionalObligations: Use public ordinary controller/RPC response boundaries for dispatch-then-reset/lost-response and genuine known-not-submitted branches.
Show submitted uncertainty survives revision/epoch changes, late responses and readonly cached-status refresh.
Show one explicit execute cannot be repeated while the first outcome is unknown, and no automatic mutation is emitted.
Preserve exact selected task/version/auth binding and original authoritative reconciliation.

findings.origin: New connected gate and optional observers do not require the complete original observable capability.
findings.title: Snapshot-only state/generation stores can pass readiness without lifecycle subscriptions
sourceDerivation: Apply validates rpc/slots/layout, then connected checks only snapshot values.
Panel falls back to empty subscription functions but can still obtain connected/established snapshots.
An incomplete store shape with getSnapshot and no subscribe can permit fresh worker decision controls with no lifecycle invalidation observer.
The actual official original service supplies both methods; no malformed live-host observation is claimed.
findings.requiredDisposition: Require complete original state and generation observable capabilities before readiness. Missing or partial stores must remain truthfully unavailable/read-only, with no synthesized observables, fake generation or mutation of frozen transport interfaces.
functionalObligations: Distinguish complete original service, initial unknown snapshots, whole-store absence and snapshot-only stores.
Show incomplete dependencies cannot enable decisions even with connected/established snapshot values.
Keep readonly recovery reachable without treating incomplete observables as authority.

positiveSourceContracts.claim: The new state/generation observer and queued setup read follow the actual original controller/wrapper/Gateway ordering.
Synchronous establishment and Gateway reset coalesce into one queued readonly setup refresh; active and current connected snapshots are checked before the read.
Fresh idle setup readiness leads to task list/detail refresh before cached worker status; the revision is captured after synchronous setup loading publication.
Unchanged revision/epoch/abort guards suppress stale readonly results. Later reset and disposal invalidate pending follow-ups.
positiveSourceContracts.limit: Does not settle mutations or resolve F-WRC02.

positiveSourceContracts.claim: New lifecycle reads setup status, task list/details and cached workerStatus. It invokes no automatic grant, policy confirmation, context preparation, worker creation, execution, capture or finish.
positiveSourceContracts.limit: This is text/source analysis, not captured runtime effects.

positiveSourceContracts.claim: The new worker-card decision gate requires actual connected/generation snapshots and enabled fresh nonbusy status. Failed refresh retains stale/unavailable; cached status alone cannot pass the gate.
positiveSourceContracts.limit: Incomplete observable capability is F-WRC03; in-flight mutation uncertainty is F-WRC02.

positiveSourceContracts.claim: Retained task/version/auth selection invalidation and explicit preview/accept/grant gates remain; terminal, cancellation-requested and recovery-required tasks do not become worker execution tasks merely by refreshing status.
positiveSourceContracts.limit: No claim that every native/currentness/All87 criterion is proved.

positiveSourceContracts.claim: No original controller, Gateway, connection loop, generation source or frozen transport interface is replaced or mutated; genuine original store arrow methods can be passed without changing their receiver.
positiveSourceContracts.limit: Cached status is observation, not native permission or fresh catalog proof.
